title: Can we boost the immune system?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: an expression used in spoken English in order to avoid bad luck
minor illnesses that affect your nose
an expression used in conversation to ask someone to say something to support your opinion
(something) likely to be negatively affected by something

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是BBC学英语的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Georgie. And I'm Neil. In this programme we're talking about the immune system, which is the body's natural defence against getting ill.
sentences.zh: 我是Georgie。我是Neil。在这个节目中我们讨论免疫系统，它是身体对抗生病的天然防御系统。

sentences.en: Now, Georgie, is there anything you do to boost your immune system?
sentences.zh: 那么，Georgie，你有什么方法来增强你的免疫系统吗？

sentences.en: Yes. I try to eat lots of oranges, which apparently have lots of vitamin C, and there are lots of things people do to try to improve their immune system, and stay healthier, like eating certain foods, taking vitamins, or even activities like swimming in cold water.
sentences.zh: 有。我尽量吃很多橙子，显然它们含有大量的维生素C，人们会做很多事情来尝试改善他们的免疫系统，保持更健康，比如吃特定的食物、服用维生素，甚至像冷水游泳这样的活动。

sentences.en: We'll find out how useful some of these techniques are in today's programme.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中我们将探讨其中一些技巧有多大用处。

sentences.en: But first, Georgie, a question. We all know the common cold – now, that’s the illness that makes you cough and sneeze, have a sore throat and headache.
sentences.zh: 但首先，Georgie，有个问题。我们都知道普通感冒——也就是那种让你咳嗽、打喷嚏、喉咙痛和头疼的疾病。

sentences.en: But how many colds does the average adult get in the UK each year?
sentences.zh: 但在英国，成年人平均每年得多少次感冒？

sentences.en: Is it: a) 2-3? b) 4-5? Or c) 7-8? Eight would be a lot.
sentences.zh: 是：a) 2-3次？ b) 4-5次？ 还是 c) 7-8次？ 八次可就太多了。

sentences.en: I'm going to go with a) 2-3 colds a year.
sentences.zh: 我选 a) 一年2-3次感冒。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out at the end of the programme if you're right.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们在节目结束时揭晓你是否答对。

sentences.en: Now, many people can become ill over the winter with diseases like colds, flu and Covid-19.
sentences.zh: 现在，许多人在冬天会生病，得感冒、流感和新冠肺炎等疾病。

sentences.en: Host of BBC Radio 4 programme Inside Health, James Gallagher, gathered some experts to talk about immune systems, and he started off by asking whether they'd had more illnesses than usual this winter.
sentences.zh: BBC Radio 4节目Inside Health的主持人James Gallagher聚集了一些专家来谈论免疫系统，他首先询问他们今年冬天生病的频率是否比平时多。

sentences.en: Hello! [Hi.] Right, how has everyone been this winter?
sentences.zh: 你好！[嗨。]好啦，大家这个冬天过得怎么样？

sentences.en: Because I've had a rotten one and I have felt constantly ill since about November.
sentences.zh: 因为我过得很糟糕，从大约11月份开始我就觉得一直在生病。

sentences.en: John? I have not had anything yet, touch wood.
sentences.zh: John？我还没生过病，敲木头求好运。

sentences.en: OK, let's see what I can infect you with by the end of the show.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们看看节目结束前我能把什么传染给你。

sentences.en: Margaret? I was pretty unwell in September.
sentences.zh: Margaret？我9月份的时候病得挺重。

sentences.en: I had what I presume to be Covid. But I've been alright since, mild snuffles aside.
sentences.zh: 我得了我猜应该是新冠的病。不过之后除了有点轻微流鼻涕之外，我一直挺好的。

sentences.en: Eleanor, I really need someone to back me up.
sentences.zh: Eleanor，我真的需要有人支持我。

sentences.en: No, sorry, I've been absolutely 100% tickety-boo.
sentences.zh: 不，不好意思，我完全100%好得很。

sentences.en: Unlike James, Professor John Tregoning hasn't been ill.
sentences.zh: 和James不同，John Tregoning教授并没有生病。

sentences.en: John uses the expression touch wood, which is an informal phrase said in order to avoid bad luck.
sentences.zh: John用了touch wood这个表达，这是一个用来避免霉运的非正式短语。

sentences.en: Doctor Margaret McCartney was unwell in September but has only had a few snuffles since.
sentences.zh: Margaret McCartney医生在9月份时生病了，但之后只有几次轻微流鼻涕。

sentences.en: Snuffles is an informal word used to describe minor illnesses that affect your nose.
sentences.zh: Snuffles是一个非正式词汇，用来描述影响鼻子的轻微疾病。

sentences.en: We can also say sniffles. Host James is surprised that nobody has been ill, and says to Professor Eleanor Riley ' back me up '.
sentences.zh: 我们也可以说sniffles。主持人James很惊讶没有人生病，并对Eleanor Riley教授说‘back me up’。

sentences.en: If you ask someone to back you up, you are asking for them to say something which supports your opinion.
sentences.zh: 如果你让别人back you up，你是在请求他们说一些支持你观点的话。

sentences.en: But Eleanor has had a healthy winter too.
sentences.zh: 但Eleanor这个冬天也很健康。

sentences.en: She's been tickety-boo, which is an informal phrase meaning everything's fine or in good order.
sentences.zh: 她一直tickety-boo，这是一个非正式短语，意思是万事大吉或状况良好。

sentences.en: Throughout the winter, many people try different techniques, like taking supplements or eating certain foods to boost their immune system, to improve their body's natural defences against disease.
sentences.zh: 整个冬天，许多人尝试不同的技巧，比如吃补充剂或特定食物来增强免疫系统，以提高身体对疾病的天然防御能力。

sentences.en: Host of BBC Radio 4's Inside Health James Gallagher asks doctor Margaret McCartney whether some of these products are successful.
sentences.zh: BBC Radio 4的Inside Health主持人James Gallagher询问Margaret McCartney医生其中一些产品是否管用。

sentences.en: OK quick-fire round Margaret. Echinacea?
sentences.zh: 好的，快问快答环节，Margaret。紫锥菊？

sentences.en: No. Turmeric? No. Ginger shots? No. This is a very, very good quiz!
sentences.zh: 没有。姜黄？没有。生姜汁？没有。这是一个非常非常好的测验！

sentences.en: What about the stuff you squirt up your nose when you're at the beginning of an infection?
sentences.zh: 那你生病初期喷鼻子那些东西呢？

sentences.en: Interesting, but not any better than normal saline spray – just salt water.
sentences.zh: 有意思，但并不比普通生理盐水喷雾——也就是盐水——更好。

sentences.en: In fact, according to Margaret, there isn't enough evidence that many popular health products can actually change the way your immune system works.
sentences.zh: 事实上，根据Margaret的说法，没有足够的证据表明许多流行的健康产品真的能改变你免疫系统的工作方式。

sentences.en: Another popular health trend in the UK is cold water swimming.
sentences.zh: 英国另一个流行的健康趋势是冷水游泳。

sentences.en: People who swim in cold water say it's good for their mental health, and they also believe it makes them less likely to get ill during the winter months.
sentences.zh: 在冷水游泳的人说这对他们的心理健康有好处，他们还相信这能让他们在冬季不太容易生病。

sentences.en: But scientists aren't sure about the benefits of cold water swimming for the immune system yet, as Professor John Tregoning explains to BBC Radio 4’s Inside Health.
sentences.zh: 但科学家们还不确定冷水游泳对免疫系统是否有益，正如John Tregoning教授向BBC Radio 4的Inside Health所解释的那样。

sentences.en: The social element actually is really important.
sentences.zh: 社交元素其实非常重要。

sentences.en: It probably is beneficial to do. You reduce stress and cortisol dampens the immune system, so actually if you're stressed then maybe you are more prone to infection.
sentences.zh: 这样做可能确实有益。你减少了压力，而皮质醇会削弱免疫系统，所以实际上如果你感到压力大，那你可能更容易受到感染。

sentences.en: And that may be why that benefit of being with people, nice people that you like in nice places, is helping.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是和人们在一起的好处所在，在美好的地方和喜欢的好人在一起有所帮助。

sentences.en: But I don’t think it's unique to cold water swimming.
sentences.zh: 但我不认为这是冷水游泳独有的。

sentences.en: I think you could probably get it from dancing or singing or going for a run.
sentences.zh: 我想你大概可以通过跳舞、唱歌或跑步来获得这种效果。

sentences.en: John says that cortisol, a chemical associated with stress, dampens the immune system.
sentences.zh: John说皮质醇是一种与压力相关的化学物质，会削弱免疫系统。

sentences.en: Here, dampens means makes weaker. We also have a common expression ' dampen someone’s spirits ' which means to make them less enthusiastic about something.
sentences.zh: 在这里，dampens的意思是使变弱。我们还有一个常用表达'dampen someone’s spirits'，意思是让某人对某事失去热情。

sentences.en: John says that there is evidence that people who are stressed are more prone to infection.
sentences.zh: John说有证据表明压力大的人更容易受到感染。

sentences.en: If you're more prone to something, it’s more likely to happen to you.
sentences.zh: 如果你更容易招惹某种情况，它就更有可能发生在你身上。

sentences.en: It could be that cold water swimming reduces stress, and so it helps people’s immune systems work well.
sentences.zh: 可能是冷水游泳减轻了压力，从而帮助人们的免疫系统良好运作。

sentences.en: But there are lots of other activities that could have the same effect, and help people have fewer colds over winter.
sentences.zh: 但还有许多其他活动可以产生同样的效果，并帮助人们在冬天减少感冒。

sentences.en: Which reminds me of my question, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了我的问题，Georgie。

sentences.en: I asked how many colds the average UK adult has a year.
sentences.zh: 我问英国成年人平均一年感冒几次。

sentences.en: And I said 2-3. And that is the correct answer, so well done!
sentences.zh: 而我说是2-3次。这就是正确答案，所以干得漂亮！

sentences.en: Thank you! OK, let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with touch wood, which is an expression used, often in speech, to avoid bad luck.
sentences.zh: 谢谢！好的，让我们回顾一下我们学过的新词，从touch wood开始，这是一个经常在口语中使用的表达，用来避免霉运。

sentences.en: Snuffles, or sniffles, are minor illnesses that affect your nose.
sentences.zh: Snuffles，或者sniffles，是影响你鼻子的轻微疾病。

sentences.en: If you ask someone to back you up, you want them to say something to support your opinion.
sentences.zh: 如果你让别人back you up，你是想让他们说些话来支持你的观点。

sentences.en: The expression tickety-boo means fine and in good order.
sentences.zh: 表达tickety-boo的意思是很好且状况良好。

sentences.en: If you dampen something you make it weaker.
sentences.zh: 如果你dampen某事，你就是让它变弱。

sentences.en: And the expression dampen someone's spirits means you make them less enthusiastic about something.
sentences.zh: 而表达dampen someone's spirits的意思是你让某人对某事不那么热情了。

sentences.en: And if you're more prone to something, it's more likely to happen to you.
sentences.zh: 如果你对某事更prone，它就更有可能发生在你身上。

sentences.en: Once again our 6 minutes are up, but you can test what you've learned with the free interactive quiz on our website.
sentences.zh: 我们的6分钟又到了，不过你可以在我们网站上的免费互动测验中测试你所学的内容。

sentences.en: Bye for now. Goodbye! Thanks for listening to this podcast from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 先这样。再见！谢谢收听BBC学英语的这个播客。

sentences.en: Continue your learning on our website with courses, quizzes and programmes to improve your English.
sentences.zh: 在我们的网站上继续学习课程、测验和节目来提高你的英语。

sentences.en: Visit bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 访问bbclearningenglish.com。
